newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan fund raises loans to farmers by 47 percent.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan fund raises loans to farmers by 47 percent.

text.p: Morocco's agriculture fund Caisse Nationale de Credit Agricole (CNCA) said on Monday it had lifted the ceiling on loans to farmers by up to 47 percent to $291 per hectare to help modernise agriculture.

"To boost Morocco's agricultural output and extend irrigated surfaces, mainly in dry areas, CNCA decided to increase loans to farmers to up to 2,500 dirhams ($291) per hectare in 1996/97," the official MAP news agency quoted fund director Abdallah Lahlou as saying.
In the 1995/96 season loans were set at a maximum 1,700 dirhams per hectare, MAP said.
"Loans, which were devoted to a total of 100,000 projects from September 1995 to June 1996, totalled 500 million dirhams," Lahlou added.
CNCA is a fund owned by the state and its managing director is appointed by King Hassan.
Farmers' debt to the fund has dropped to 4.5 billion dirhams in 1995/96 season from 8.0 billion dirhams in the previous season, Lahlou said.
Between the 1990/91 and 1994/95 seasons, useable farm land reached around 9.2 million hectares, 55 percent of which was under cereals, the agriculture ministry said in a recent report.
Morocco plans to increase irrigated land to 1.33 million hectares by the year 2020, it said.

By then, Moroccan farmers should be able to produce 29 million quintals (2.9 million tonnes) of wheat on irrigated land -- one quarter of the country's total production -- and 100 percent of its sugar production, the ministry added.
